classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the masses need matching units, convert tonnes to kilograms, and apply percentage change using the birth mass as the original amount.

content.prompt:
An elephant calf weighed 115 kg when born. The calf grew to an adult weighing 5.93 tonnes.
Calculate the percentage change in mass, to the nearest whole percent.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Final mass}&=5.93\times1000\text{ kg}\\\text{Final mass}&=5930\text{ kg}\\\text{Change in mass}&=5930-115\\\text{Change in mass}&=5815\text{ kg}\\\text{Percentage change}&=\frac{5815}{115}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage change}&\approx5057\%\end{align*}$$
The positive change represents an increase.
